report.summary: Payment failures began at 10:00 UTC, right after payment-service's connection-acquire timeout was cut from 5000 ms to 50 ms at 09:58 UTC (config change C09). Payment-service logs show its payments-db pool saturated (active=12, idle=0, waiting=31) and timing out at 50 ms, which returns 503s to checkout. The database itself looks healthy (connections flat, query latency normal), so the fault appears to be the client-side timeout change rather than database capacity. Confidence is high but not fully verified: no direct test of the timeout value was run, and checkout's full error volume is only partly visible.

root_cause.mechanism: Reducing db.pool.connection_timeout_ms from 5000 to 50 ms at 09:58 causes requests waiting for a payments-db pool connection (active=12, waiting=31) to time out, returning 503s to checkout, while the DB itself stays healthy.
assumptions: The config key controls the acquire timeout for the payments-db pool.

ranked_hypotheses.mechanism: Reducing db.pool.connection_timeout_ms from 5000 to 50 ms at 09:58 causes requests waiting for a payments-db pool connection (active=12, waiting=31) to time out, returning 503s to checkout, while the DB itself stays healthy.
assumptions: The config key controls the acquire timeout for the payments-db pool.

ranked_hypotheses.mechanism: Connection or capacity exhaustion on payments-db slows connection grants so the pool times out.
assumptions: The DB-side pool limit is not visible in the metrics.

ranked_hypotheses.mechanism: External provider slowness or errors cause payment-service 5xx and checkout failures.
assumptions: Provider-side errors would show as provider response timeouts; only 2 such log lines were seen.

observed_facts.statement: A config change set payment-service db.pool.connection_timeout_ms from 5000 to 50 (ticket OPS-2291, by j.alvarez) at 09:58:00Z.
payment-service error_rate jumped from ~0.2% (09:55 point 0.25%) to 28.43% at 10:00:00Z and stayed 25-29% through 10:30.
payment-service latency_p99 dropped from ~433-461 ms to ~135-145 ms starting 10:00:00Z.
payment-service logs show 45 'Timeout acquiring connection from pool payments-db after 50ms (active=12, idle=0, waiting=31)' errors, first at 10:00:17Z.
checkout-service error_rate rose from ~0.3% to 12.45% at 10:00:00Z, and its logs show 'payment-service call failed: 503 Service Unavailable' starting 10:00:19Z.
payments-db connections stayed at 116-125 throughout 09:00-10:30, with query_latency_p99 about 11.5-12.5 ms and replication lag about 0.4 s.
payment-service CPU (~32-34%) and memory (~53-57%) were flat across the window.
payments-db health check reports 'accepting connections; SELECT 1 ok' at 10:28Z; payment-service /health returned 200.
Only 3 'insufficient funds' declines appear in payment-service logs in the window, spread across 09:40-10:02.

Other changes in the prior 3 days (inventory v4.1.9, search v5.3.1, payment v3.1.3 on 09-01 04:00, checkout v2.13.4 on 09-01 14:00, node pool upgrade 09-02 01:00) all predate the 10:00 onset by many hours.

assumptions: The 50 ms value is applied to the payments-db pool acquire timeout in payment-service (the config key name implies this), and the change took effect at 09:58 with no other concurrent changes.
Connection acquisition waits are normally well below 50 ms under the ~60 req/s load, so the reduced timeout causes failures even without database slowness.
payments-db health checks are shallow and do not measure pool-level or write-path behaviour.
Checkout's 12% error rate reflects payment 503s propagating without a retry that masks them, so checkout's error count is not fully visible in the sampled logs.

inferred_conclusions.statement: The root cause is the 09:58 config change reducing payment-service's payments-db connection acquire timeout from 5000 ms to 50 ms, which makes normal pool waits exceed the timeout and produces 503s that propagate to checkout.
A genuine payments-db capacity or connection exhaustion problem is unlikely, since DB connections, CPU and query latency stayed flat while errors spiked.
The 'insufficient funds' declines are background noise and not the cause of the 5xx spike.
Reverting the timeout to 5000 ms should restore payment success, since latency was normal before the change.

remediation.action: Revert db.pool.connection_timeout_ms on payment-service from 50 back to 5000 ms (roll back OPS-2291 change).
remediation.rationale: The change at 09:58 directly precedes the 10:00 onset; reverting is the fastest mitigation.

remediation.action: Confirm recovery: payment-service error_rate returns below 1% and checkout 503 warnings stop.
remediation.rationale: Verifies the hypothesis and the mitigation.

remediation.action: Review OPS-2291 with the author before any further tail-latency tuning; the reduced timeout traded latency for hard failures.
remediation.rationale: Changing a timeout that gates pool acquisition should be load-tested first.

remediation.action: Add a config-change guard or canary requirement for payment-service DB pool settings.
remediation.rationale: Prevents a single-value change from taking down the payment path.

remediation.action: Add pool-wait and acquire-timeout alerts on payment-service, and a deep health check that exercises a pool acquire and write.
remediation.rationale: Current /health and DB SELECT 1 checks stayed green during a full outage.

open_questions: Was the 50 ms value meant for a different pool or environment, and what was the intended effect on tail latency?
Why does checkout's error rate (12%) sit well below payment-service's (28%); is there retry or fallback masking the failures?
Did the change in fact take effect on all payment-service replicas, or only some?
Is there any 09:58-10:00 DB-side event not visible in the sampled metrics?
